Scheme: Stockholm congestion tax (trial Jan to Jul 2006)
Outcome_metric: Road use (traffic) inside the charging cordon during trial
Peer_reviewed_citation: Johansson, C., Burman, L., & Forsberg, B. (2009). The effects of congestions tax on air quality and health. Atmospheric Environment, 43(31), 4843-4854.
Stringency_note: Trial 3 Jan to 31 Jul 2006; weekday charge up to 20 SEK (2.2 EUR) at rush hour, max 60 SEK per day (per abstract)
Extractor_notes: Additional distinct estimate from a paper already in the database (existing row is NOx emissions). Abstract states road use within the cordon fell by about 15%; no counterfactual control, figure is taken from trial traffic evaluation data. Approximate value ('about').

Outcome_metric: Total road traffic PM10 emissions in charged inner city (modelled from traffic change)
Peer_reviewed_citation: Johansson, C., Burman, L., & Forsberg, B. (2009). The effects of congestions tax on air quality and health. Atmospheric Environment, 43(31), 4843-4854.
Stringency_note: Trial 3 Jan to 31 Jul 2006; weekday charge up to 20 SEK (2.2 EUR) at rush hour, max 60 SEK per day (per abstract)
Extractor_notes: Additional pollutant from a paper already in the database (companion to existing NOx emissions -8.5% row). Emission change, not ambient concentration; emission model applied to observed traffic change.

Outcome_metric: Annual mean ambient NOx concentration on most densely trafficked inner-city streets (dispersion model, permanent scheme)
Peer_reviewed_citation: Johansson, C., Burman, L., & Forsberg, B. (2009). The effects of congestions tax on air quality and health. Atmospheric Environment, 43(31), 4843-4854.
Stringency_note: Trial 3 Jan to 31 Jul 2006; weekday charge up to 20 SEK (2.2 EUR) at rush hour, max 60 SEK per day (per abstract)
Extractor_notes: Upper bound ('up to 12%'): dispersion-modelled annual effect if trial traffic changes were made permanent; not a measured concentration change. Greater Stockholm population-weighted NOx exposure fell 0.23 ug/m3 (no baseline in abstract, so no %). Treat as lower-quality evidence; drop if only measured concentrations are wanted.

Outcome_metric: Annual mean ambient PM10 concentration on most densely trafficked inner-city streets (dispersion model, permanent scheme)
Peer_reviewed_citation: Johansson, C., Burman, L., & Forsberg, B. (2009). The effects of congestions tax on air quality and health. Atmospheric Environment, 43(31), 4843-4854.
Stringency_note: Trial 3 Jan to 31 Jul 2006; weekday charge up to 20 SEK (2.2 EUR) at rush hour, max 60 SEK per day (per abstract)
Extractor_notes: Upper bound ('up to 7%'): dispersion-modelled annual effect if trial traffic changes were made permanent; not a measured concentration change. Abstract notes PM10 and NO2 limit values still exceeded on busiest streets.

Outcome_metric: Traffic volume across cordon, whole day (24 h incl. non-charged hours), after vs before Jan 2013
Peer_reviewed_citation: West, J., & Börjesson, M. (2020). The Gothenburg congestion charges: cost-benefit analysis and distribution effects. Transportation, 47(1), 145-174.
Extractor_notes: Observed average reduction in cordon traffic ('on average ten per cent'); footnote says 24 h figure including non-charged hours, so distinct from the charged-hours -12% in Börjesson & Kristoffersson (2015), but likely the same City of Gothenburg counts; avoid double counting in pooling. No control group. Same paper: observed travel times on inner arterials -9%; public transport ridership +7% 2012 to 2013 (about 5% attributed to charges). Model forecast was -9% cordon traffic. Online 2018, print 2020. Open access full text.

Scheme: Stockholm congestion tax (end of green-vehicle exemption, 1 Jul 2012)
Outcome_metric: Morning (06:30 to 12:00) weekday cordon crossings by previously exempt green-vehicle commuters, May to June 2013 vs 2012
Peer_reviewed_citation: Naqavi, F., Engström, E., & Franklin, J. P. (2023). Green vehicles' responses to an expiring congestion toll exemption: Findings from a natural experiment in Stockholm, Sweden. Findings.
Stringency_note: Exemption for older green vehicles phased out 1 July 2012; conventional vehicles always charged
Extractor_notes: Crossings 69,563 to 46,764 in ANPR panel (2,076 green-vehicle commuters); Wilcoxon p<0.001. Comparison group: conventional-vehicle commuters 13,051 to 13,868 crossings (+6.3%, computed; not significant p=0.08). Authors use non-parametric tests, not a formal DiD regression, so coded Before-after with comparison group. Effect is of extending the charge to a vehicle subgroup, not of the scheme as a whole; years counted from permanent scheme Aug 2007 (about 0.9 years after exemption ended). Authors note exempt status not fully observed, so effect may be understated.
